title: Functions via Formulas
summary: Function notation $f(x)$ evaluates and combines formulas. Evaluating at expressions, and computing the difference quotient $\dfrac{f(x+h)-f(x)}{h}$, prepares the ground for calculus and reveals average rates of change.

function notation.in_class: $f(3)$ means the output when the input is 3.

average rate of change.plain: Slope between two points on a graph.

piecewise function.in_class: Choose the branch matching the input.

input expression.plain: Plugging an expression (not just a number) into $f$.

linear function.plain: A function with a constant rate of change.

concept_sections.heading: Function notation
concept_sections.explanation: $f(x)$ names the output for input $x$. To evaluate $f(a)$, substitute $a$ for every $x$ and simplify.

concept_sections.heading: Evaluating at expressions
concept_sections.explanation: You can input whole expressions: $f(x+h)$ means replace $x$ with $(x+h)$ throughout, keeping parentheses to avoid sign errors.

concept_sections.heading: Average rate of change
concept_sections.explanation: Between $x=a$ and $x=b$, the average rate is $\dfrac{f(b)-f(a)}{b-a}$ — the slope of the secant line.
math_steps: Divide the output change by the input change.

concept_sections.heading: The difference quotient
concept_sections.explanation: $\dfrac{f(x+h)-f(x)}{h}$ generalizes the average rate over a small step $h$. Simplifying it (canceling $h$) is the key precalculus-to-calculus skill.

concept_sections.heading: Piecewise functions
concept_sections.explanation: A piecewise function uses different rules on different intervals. To evaluate, first find which interval the input lies in, then use that branch.

real_world_examples.title: A cell phone plan
real_world_examples.scenario: Cost jumps after a data cap.
real_world_examples.how_the_math_applies: The bill is a piecewise function: one rate below the cap, another above.

real_world_examples.title: Average speed of a trip
real_world_examples.how_the_math_applies: The average rate of change of position gives the trip's average speed.

real_world_examples.title: Slope of a hill
real_world_examples.scenario: Rise over run between two markers.
real_world_examples.how_the_math_applies: The difference quotient measures the average steepness between points.
